transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-30 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood), Raj Patel (CTO, ZenPort), Sofia Alvarez (ML Engineer), Dana Kim (Infra Ops), Ethan Brooks (Product)

Auto-summary: Discussed Dedicated capacity needs for ZenPort's inference workloads. Focus on reserved GPUs, isolation, burst handling, and next steps for POC and security review.

[00:00] Maria Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really quick intro, I'm Maria, AE on the account, with Liam our solutions engineer, Priya is on for ops.
[00:12] Raj Patel: Thanks Maria, appreciate it. We are evaluating a few options — curiosity on how Redwood's Dedicated offering handles reserved GPU pools and burst patterns.
[00:25] Liam O'Connor: Yep, happy to walk through that. Can you give us a bit of context on current infra? What models, peak QPS, latency targets?
[00:35] Sofia Alvarez: Sure, right now we're running internal BERT-ish retrieval + a 7B generative model for chat, roughly 40 req/s steady across europe and north america, peaks to about 220 req/s during end of day routing. Latency SLO is sub 300ms p50 for short prompts, p95 we target 800ms.
[00:50] Dana Kim: Our security posture is strict, we need VPC isolation, SAML SSO integration, and audit logs retained for 12 months. Also key management via our HSM/KMS.
[01:05] Maria Chen: That's great context. For Dedicated we do reserved GPU pools — you can commit to a pool size, that's isolated to your tenant and network. We support VPC peering or private link and customer-managed KMS. Audit logs are available and retention is configurable.
[01:25] Raj Patel: On the reserved pool: how does burst work? We sometimes see sudden spikes for routing during shipments. We don't want to overcommit monthly but need headroom.
[01:38] Liam O'Connor: Good question. We offer a burst policy: you reserve a baseline pool and can configure burst capacity which can draw from spare capacity in the region or your dedicated burst buffer. There are two flavors — short-term regional burst (best-effort, cheaper) and guaranteed emergency burst you pay for as pre-warmed nodes. We can show numbers in the pricing sheet.
[01:55] Sofia Alvarez: If we use region burst, what's the latency impact? We can't have a jump at p95 over 1s.
[02:05] Liam O'Connor: Region burst may route to other nodes with slightly higher cold start, but we also have KV cache pre-warming and continuous batching to smooth token generation. Realistically, for your p95 goal we'd recommend a small guaranteed burst buffer sized to cover 99th percentile spikes.
[02:24] Raj Patel: You mentioned KV cache, sorry I heard KV cash earlier in the docs — can you clarify?
[02:30] Liam O'Connor: Yeah, sorry transcription — KV cache, it's the key-value cache for transformer past key values. It lets you reuse cache for multi-turn chat so subsequent calls are much faster and cheaper.
[02:45] Ethan Brooks: On model pinning — can we pin a specific model version across rollout? We have strict QA for model changes.
[02:52] Maria Chen: Absolutely, Dedicated supports model version pinning and canary rollouts. You can route a percentage of traffic to a canary and auto-fallback if regression is detected.
[03:05] Dana Kim: For network isolation, do you support on-prem option or only VPC?
[03:12] Maria Chen: Both. We have Private deployments for full on-prem/air-gapped environments and Dedicated in VPC for most enterprise customers. For Private we provide a control plane that you can host; there are additional licensing and deployment windows.
[03:26] Sofia Alvarez: For the POC, we'd prefer Dedicated in our VPC first to validate performance, then evaluate Private if we need on-prem.
[03:35] Liam O'Connor: That makes sense. For the POC we'll size a baseline pool — can you share the traffic profile and some representative prompts? That lets us recommend baseline and burst sizing.
[03:45] Sofia Alvarez: We'll send anonymized prompt sets and traffic histogram. Expect something with median seq len ~80 tokens, but there are some long docs to 1200 tokens occasionally.
[03:56] Maria Chen: Long sequences affect memory and GPU selection — we'll likely recommend mixed instance types. Also, about quantization: if you plan to use int8 we can provide profiles, but some long-context models prefer fp16.
[04:12] Raj Patel: How do you price burst usage vs reserved? Is it per-token or per-node-hour?
[04:18] Maria Chen: Reserved baseline is a node-hour commit. Burst can be configured as node-hour on-demand at a premium, or a pre-warmed buffer you reserve for shorter term. We price egress and tokenization separately. We'll share the detailed spreadsheet.
[04:33] Ethan Brooks: Security/compliance — we use SOC2 plus internal PCI-like controls, do you have SOC2 and ISO certs?
[04:40] Maria Chen: Yes, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. For Dedicated we can provide audit logs, SAML SSO, RBAC, and we support customer-managed KMS and VPC-only egress.
[04:55] Dana Kim: Do you integrate with our existing KMS (HashiCorp Vault)?
[05:00] Liam O'Connor: We have KMS integrations for AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and customer HSM via standard interfaces — HashiCorp Vault can be integrated through HSM/KMS bridging. We'll note integration steps in the security deep dive.
[05:16] Raj Patel: Operationally, how about autoscaling? We need predictable scaling without noisy neighbor effects.
[05:24] Liam O'Connor: Dedicated autoscaling is policy-driven. You can set SLO-based scaling (scale on p95 latency crossing threshold), queue-depth scaling, or schedule-based scaling. Because it's reserved capacity per tenant, noisy neighbor is minimized compared to public endpoints. We also support vertical scaling of model variants.
[05:42] Sofia Alvarez: Can we use mixed precision and quantized models? We run some experiments with int8 and 4-bit.
[05:49] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we support quantized runtimes — some models run better with q4_0 or q8 depending on the architecture. We'll recommend model-specific quant profiles in the POC. Note sometimes quantization impacts output quality; Redwood Optimize can run regressions against your evals.
[06:07] Maria Chen: Quick check — anyone blocked on procurement terms or need legal/PO?
[06:12] Raj Patel: Procurement's standard, but our budget ops prefer monthly committed vs annual. We'll figure out commitments after POC.
[06:20] Maria Chen: Understood. We'll include pricing options for monthly and annual commits.
[06:26] Ethan Brooks: For the POC, do you provide telemetry access? We want per-route latency and token-level cost breakdowns.
[06:33] Liam O'Connor: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, per-model/per-route dashboards, traces and error analysis. For Dedicated we can configure dashboard access and longer retention as an add-on.
[06:46] Dana Kim: One more on data residency — can we restrict model hosting to eu-west only?
[06:51] Maria Chen: Yes you can pin regionally and set routing policies to keep traffic in region, and we can disable cross-region fallbacks for strict residency.
[07:02] Sofia Alvarez: Regarding benchmarks, how will you measure p95 vs cost?
[07:08] Liam O'Connor: We'll run a synthetic benchmark using your prompt set and traffic histogram, measure throughput, latencies p50/p95, and provide cost per 1M tokens under baseline and burst. We'll also run variant tests with quantized models.
[07:21] Raj Patel: Sounds good. Any blockers for scheduling the security deep dive? Dana is the point there.
[07:27] Dana Kim: Week of Dec 8 works for us. We'll compile our required docs ahead.
[07:33] Maria Chen: Great — recap of next steps: Maria sends pricing + burst policy spreadsheet; Liam drafts benchmark plan; Sofia sends traffic/profile; Dana schedules security deep dive.
[07:46] Ethan Brooks: Thanks team, looking forward to the POC.
[07:50] Maria Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to the pricing sheet and a shared folder for prompt sets.
